items.q: Why does Huberman treat time perception as so central?
items.a: **Perception of time** is "perhaps the most important factor in how we gauge our life" — it shapes **mood, stress, happiness**, and how we judge past, present, and future.

items.q: How do you keep your body clock locked to the outside world?
items.a: View **10–30 min bright light** (ideally sun) within ~**1 hour of waking** and again afternoon/evening; minimize evening bright light; exercise at consistent times. Circadian misalignment raises risks for cancer, obesity, mental health, and hormone disruption.

items.q: How long can the brain stay in deep focus?
items.a: About **90 minutes** — an ultradian block where acetylcholine/dopamine support focus, then circuits resist further deep work. You **choose when a cycle starts**; it is not tied to sleep-cycle end.

items.q: How many hard 90-minute blocks should you schedule per day?
items.a: Max about **2 hard blocks/day**, separated by **2–4 hours**. These are for hard problem-solving — not email/social — and even one block still feels taxing.

items.q: How does dopamine change how fast time feels?
items.a: More dopamine → you **overestimate** elapsed time (a minute called at ~**38 seconds**). Dopamine/NE run higher in the **first half of the day**, so schedule hardest work **morning**.

items.q: What does serotonin do to the time clock?
items.a: Serotonin tends to make you **underestimate** time. It rises in the **evening** and supports the sleep transition — opposite direction from morning dopamine/NE.

items.q: What breaks first when sleep is disrupted?
items.a: Daily regulation of **dopamine, norepinephrine, and serotonin** — the neuromodulators that fine-slice or batch your sense of time and work capacity.

items.q: Why does a fun day feel short now but long later?
items.a: High-dopamine **fun/variety feels fast now, long later**; boredom feels **slow now, short later**. Two stopwatches: fine-sliced encoding vs big memory bins (the amusement-park paradox).

items.q: Why are traumatic memories so sticky and slow-motion?
items.a: **Overclocking**: huge dopamine/NE spikes make you perceive ultra slow motion and stamp the hippocampus at a **high frame rate**. Dopamine here is **motivation/arousal**, not "reward."

items.q: How does novelty stretch how long a place or relationship feels?
items.a: More **novel places, people, and experiences** expand retrospective time — e.g. three apartments + 3× people + 3× experiences in NYC can feel like you've lived there longer than one apartment/year.

items.q: How do habits carve up your day?
items.a: Anchor routines at **fixed day intervals** so they release dopamine and become **functional time bins** — morning habit + meal habits segment experience beyond mere convenience.
